newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Manila says not surprised if Soros led peso attack.
newsitem.headline: Manila says not surprised if Soros led peso attack.

text.p: Philippine Finance Secretary Roberto de Ocampo said on Monday he would not be surprised if American financier George Soros was behind the recent speculative attack on the peso.

"George Soros has done this before ... So it would come as no surprise if he really was part of it," de Ocampo said. He was replying to a question from reporters before attending a state of the nation address from President Fidel Ramos.

Last Saturday, Malaysian Prime Minister Mahathir Mohamad named Soros as the man responsible for the recent shake-up of the currencies in the south east Asia, an allegation denied by the U.S. State Department.
De Ocampo said there was no evidence that would implicate Soros in speculation against the peso which forced the central bank to allow a de facto devaluation on July 11.
De Ocampo went on to say that the Philippines should not be embroiled in witch-hunting as "we have to recognise that movements like these are now part of the global financial environment."
"And the best preparation against these, of course, is to have a strong economy and a sensible foreign exchange policy," he added.
